summary: Vintage video-game cartridges, discs, and consoles with sustained $100+ resale floors. Focus on RARE and CIB (Complete-In-Box) titles where the cart alone trades $50-2000+, plus museum-tier sealed apex pieces ($1K-100K+). Loose commodity cartridges (most NES / Genesis / PS1 games are $5-15) are NOT included — only the verified high-resale titles. Sweet spot: poly-mailer to small-box ship class. PriceCharting already routes video-game titles to free comp lookups; BOLO matching here surfaces these lots in the picker's brand-hint badge + the analysis-view pie chart, AND gates audit fast-skip eligibility.
field_workflow: Photograph the cartridge label clearly + the back chip-board sticker (date code + region)
CIB (Complete in Box): requires box, cartridge, manual, inserts, foam tray — all original = premium
Sealed-NEW: factory wrap intact, no V-cut, no tampering signs — collector apex (2-10x CIB)
Region matters: NTSC-U (US), NTSC-J (Japan), PAL (UK/Europe) — Japan-only releases command premium for English-speaking collectors
Cartridges with the right manufacturing chip (e.g., NES Stadium Events with the right PCB) authenticate
WATA / VGA grading slabs add 50-200% on $500+ pieces; not worth slabbing under $200
Counterfeit risk EXTREME on rare cartridges (Pokemon, Earthbound, Stadium Events) — counterfeit detection forums are a must
skip_list: Loose common cartridge (Mario / Donkey Kong / Tetris — commodity)
Damaged label / scratched disc / missing pieces
Modded / repro / reproduction cart (reproductions sold as 'reproductions' are legit but not collector-tier)
Region-locked + missing original system to play
Box without cartridge / cartridge without label
Modern reissue (Nintendo Switch Online doesn't count as vintage)
Save battery dead (kills resale 30-50% on save-game RPGs)

brands.notes: Stadium Events (Bandai 1987, very limited US distribution before licensing change) is THE NES grail — sealed/graded examples have cleared $100K+. Counterfeit risk extreme on this title; verify chip authenticity. Nintendo World Championships 1990 gray (200 produced) is the second apex. Most NES games are $5-30 commodity — only the specific names listed here warrant attention. WATA / VGA grading is worth the $80 fee on $500+ pieces.

brands.notes: Earthbound is the SNES grail — original 1995 print run was small + heavy scratch-and-sniff strategy guide makes complete sets scarce. Chrono Trigger remains the second apex (Squaresoft 1995 RPG). Donkey Kong Country Competition Cartridge (1995 Blockbuster contest, ~2500 produced) is the apex unicorn ($5K-15K). Hagane / Wild Guns / Pocky & Rocky are the late-cycle low-print-run premiums.

Insert / poster / map included = +30%

brands.notes: ClayFighter 63⅓ Sculptor's Cut (~20K produced, Blockbuster exclusive 1998) is the N64 grail. Conker's Bad Fur Day (Rare 2001) is the volume-tier rarity. Pokemon Snap / Stadium / Puzzle League CIB hold strong premium because the game is fun and the buyer pool is huge. Ogre Battle 64 is the N64 RPG apex. Verify cartridge label condition (no peeling/fading) and check the save battery on RPGs.

brands.notes: Pokemon Red/Blue/Yellow original 1998 CIB sealed-in-box is the Game Boy grail — first-print runs cleared $20K+ at peak in 2021-22 (Heritage Auctions). Counterfeit risk EXTREME — modern repro carts look identical without internal chip inspection. Mother 3 (Japan-only 2006) is the GBA apex; Boktai (with original solar-sensor cart) is the kitsch-tier rarity. Save battery condition kills RPG resale; verify by booting the cart and watching for save-corruption messages.

brands.notes: Suikoden II PS1 (Konami 1999) is the PS1 grail — small print run + cult-favorite RPG. Rule of Rose (PS2 2006, banned in some regions) is the PS2 apex; Haunting Ground sub-apex. Panzer Dragoon Saga (Saturn 1998) is the Saturn grail. Black Label distinguishes original release from Greatest Hits reprint — original always premium. Disc rot is a known issue on early-90s PS1 / Saturn discs; verify by booting before paying.

brands.notes: Sealed-in-box launch consoles command extreme premiums (NES 1985 sealed has cleared $100K+ graded). Neo Geo AES is the collector cult — SNK 1990, Japan-import-tier console at $700+ working. Limited-edition console colors (N64 Pikachu, Spice Orange GameCube, Animal Crossing Wii, Hyrule Edition Wii) are the volume-premium tier. Note: sealed-launch consoles need MEDIUM box ship — NOT poly mailer.

platform_notes.eBay: Dominant marketplace for vintage games. Use sold-listings filter — auction-style listings reveal real clearing prices.
platform_notes.Heritage Auctions: Apex marketplace for $1K+ graded sealed games. Reference for top-tier comps (Stadium Events, Pokemon, Earthbound graded).
platform_notes.PriceCharting: Already wired into the comp pipeline — provides curated freecomp lookup for vintage games. BOLO matching here is for picker visibility + audit fast-skip eligibility, not duplication of pricing.
platform_notes.WATA / VGA / CGC: Grading services for sealed games. Adds 2-10x value on $200+ titles. Submission cost $30-200 depending on tier; not worth slabbing under $200.
